raw_response:
I will not start from empty. I will start from what I did last year and only adjust a little. On my 4.1 mu, my main eating-and-cash land is still wheat-maize rotation, because here in Quzhou most people do it this way and with well water I can still push yield if the weather turns dry. I will keep most land in wheat-maize and leave a small piece for cotton, because cotton takes more watching and spraying, and at my age with only 2 people in the house I do not want too much of it. For wheat, I will put enough base fertilizer and then chase one more heavy nitrogen topdressing at jointing, because if wheat is short of fertilizer, yield falls fast and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra. For maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, enough nitrogen, and 2 irrigations if rainfall is not enough, because summer maize responds quickly when water and fertilizer are there. For cotton, I will keep only 1 mu, use improved seed, not be stingy on potash, and spray more times than grain crops because insects on cotton can ruin the field if I relax. I do watch cost, but on only 4.1 mu every missed mu of yield is real money, so I will stay close to what experienced neighbors around me do, with a little extra fertilizer rather than too little.
